The override uses `Color.Unspecified` as a sentinel and is applied **only when both colors are supplied** (`MangaButton.overrideColorsGiven`, ~line 155; `ClassicButton.overrideColors`, ~line 265). A caller that supplies just one of the pair (e.g. only `contentColor = colors.error` on a Text/Destructive action — exactly the "meaning must not follow the accent" case this API was added for) gets a silent no-op: the parameter is accepted, compiles, and renders with the theme/accent colors. That is the precise failure the comment above warns about, and it surfaces no signal. Since `Color.Transparent` is a meaningful override value (used by the new `DetailsRoot` call site), a single sentinel check is enough to make each color independent. Suggest resolving each color on its own so a lone `contentColor` is still honored:
```
val container = containerColor.takeIf { it != Color.Unspecified } ?: mangaButtonContainer(variant, colors)
val resolvedContentColor = contentColor.takeIf { it != Color.Unspecified } ?: mangaButtonContent(variant, colors, ambientInk)
```
or accept a single nullable pair/`ButtonColors` so the "all or nothing" rule is expressed by the type instead of being silently dropped at runtime.
